title: 2007 AMC 8 Problem 11
statement: Tiles \(I,\) \(II,\) \(III\) and \(IV\) are translated so one tile coincides with each of the rectangles \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C\) and \(D.\) In the final arrangement, the two numbers on any side common to two adjacent tiles must be the same. Which of the tiles is translated to Rectangle \(C?\)

solutions.text:
Only Tile \(III\) has a \(0\) on an edge, so Tile \(III\) must be placed in \(C\) or \(D\), where that edge can be on the outside.

Tile \(III\) also has a \(5\) on its right edge, and no other tile has a \(5\). Therefore Tile \(III\) must be placed in \(D\), with its \(5\) on the outside.

The only tile that can match the \(1\) on the left edge of Tile \(III\) is Tile \(IV\), so Tile \(IV\) is placed in \(C\).

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Look for edge numbers that appear on only one tile.
The \(0\) and \(5\) force the placement of Tile \(III\) before deciding which tile is in \(C\).
